lyrics:
[Intro: warm electric guitar arpeggios in six, soft organ]

[Verse 1: gentle soulful male voice]
I learned to tie a tie from a video
Learned to shave from a guy at school
Signed my own permission slips
Got good at making do

Father's Day I'd stay home sick
Never knew what card to buy
Told myself it didn't matter
I'm pretty good at lies

[Chorus: fuller, choir humming, tender]
Then you were the first to call me son
First to wait up, first to come
You knew my name before I had one
And you say it like I've already won
All those years I thought I had none
You were the first to call me son

[Verse 2: voice close, guitar and bass]
Somebody taught me a prayer one night
Starts with two words: "Our Father"
I got as far as the second one
And couldn't go any farther

'Cause the one who made the mountains
Sent his only boy for me
So a kid with no one in the bleachers
Could be family

[Chorus: fuller, choir humming, tender]
And you were the first to call me son
First to wait up, first to come
You knew my name before I had one
And you say it like I've already won
All those years I thought I had none
You were the first to call me son

[Bridge: band swells, voice breaking]
Abba. I'm still learning how to say it.
Jesus called you that in a garden, crying
Now he's teaching me. I'm trying.

[Final Chorus: full band and choir, then down to a hush]
You were the first to call me son
First to wait up, first to come
You knew my name before I had one
And you say it like I've already won
All those years I thought I had none
You were the first to call me son

[Outro: guitar alone, whispered]
Our Father...
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 58 BPM, 6/8, E-flat major. A slow, rocking soul lullaby.

VOICE: Male tenor, soft, warm and a little husky, in the style of 1960s soul sung quietly. He stays gentle until the bridge, where the voice thickens and nearly breaks. A small choir hums and then sings behind him.

INSTRUMENTS: Clean electric guitar playing arpeggios with tremolo, Hammond organ, upright-style bass, brushed drums with a soft rim click, a little piano, a choir of six voices.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and organ. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:58 Chorus 1. 1:36 Verse 2, the prayer. 2:18 Chorus 2. 2:52 Bridge. 3:10 Final chorus. 3:32 Outro, guitar and the whisper at 3:38.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Retro soul recorded warmly: tremolo guitar, tape softness, the choir in the room, nothing bright.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'I got as far as the second one and couldn't go any farther' at 1:48.

THE REVEAL: The first chorus could be about any man who stepped in. At 1:36 the prayer is the Lord's Prayer, the only boy is sent, and the bridge says Jesus used the same word, Abba, in Gethsemane.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Guarded, undone, adopted, learning to say it.
